{{nihongo|'''Takahashi Shrine'''|高椅神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

'''Takahashi Shrine''' (たかはしじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Oyama, Tochigi|Q374511|qid=Q374511}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Tochigi|af|Tochigi-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Tochigi|ar|توتشيغي (محافظة)|az|Toçiqi prefekturası|azb|توچیقی اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Tochigi|be|Татыгі (прэфектура)|bg|Точиги|bn|তোচিগি প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Tochigi|cdo|Tochigi-gâing|ce|Тотиги (префектура)|ceb|Tochigi-ken|ckb|پارێزگای تۆچیگی|cs|Prefektura Točigi|cy|Tochigi (talaith)|da|Tochigi-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Tochigi|eo|Gubernio Toĉigi|es|Prefectura de Tochigi|et|Tochigi prefektuur|eu|Tochigi (prefektura)|fa|استان توچیگی|fi|Tochigin prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Tochigi|frr|Tochigi (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Tochigi|gl|Prefectura de Tochigi|hak|Tochigi-yen|he|טוצ'יגי (מחוז)|hr|Tochigi (prefektura)|hu|Tocsigi prefektúra|hy|Տոտիգի (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Tochigi|ilo|Prepektura ti Tochigi|it|Prefettura di Tochigi|ja|栃木県|ka|ტოტიგის პრეფექტურა|kn|ತೋಚಿಗಿ (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|도치기현|lt|Točigio prefektūra|lv|Točigi prefektūra|mk|Точиги (префектура)|mni|ꯇꯣꯆꯤꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|तोचिगी प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Tochigi|mzn|توچیگی استان|ne|टोचिगी प्रदेश|nl|Tochigi (prefectuur)|no|Tochigi (prefektur)|os|Тотиги (префектурæ)|pl|Prefektura Tochigi|pnb|ضلع ٹوچیگی|pt|Tochigi|ro|Prefectura Tochigi|ru|Тотиги (префектура)|se|Tochigi prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Tochigi|si|ටොචිගි ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Tochigi Prefecture|sk|Točigi (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Точиги|su|Tochigi Prefecture|sv|Tochigi prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Tochigi|tg|Префектураи Точиги|th|จังหวัดโทจิงิ|tl|Prepektura ng Tochigi|tr|Tochigi|tt|Тотиги (префектура)|ug|توچىگى ناھىيىسى|uk|Префектура Тотіґі|ur|توچیگی پریفیکچر|vi|Tochigi|war|Tochigi (prefektura)|wuu|栃木县|zh|栃木縣|zh_classical|栃木縣|zh_min_nan|Totigi-koān|zh_yue|栃木縣|qid=Q44843}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was prefectural shrine.

It is the oldest shrine whose main deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto}}, revered as the "ancestral deity of {{ill|Cuisine|ar|مطبخ (أسلوب)|as|ৰন্ধনশৈলী|atj|Tcipakwan|ba|Аш-һыу (традициялар)|be|Кухня|bg|Кухня|bh|पकवान (इस्टाइल)|bn|রন্ধনশৈলী|br|Keginerezh|ca|Cuina|ckb|دەستاو|cs|Kuchyně (způsob přípravy jídla)|cv|Кухня (традици)|da|Kogekunst|el|Κουζίνα|eo|Kuirarto|es|Cocina (tradiciones)|eu|Sukaldaritza|fa|روش آشپزی|fi|Ruokakulttuuri|fr|Cuisine|gl|Arte culinaria|he|סגנון בישול|hi|पाकशैली|hr|Kulinarstvo|hy|Խոհանոց (ավանդույթներ)|id|Hidangan|ig|Cuisine|is|Matarhefð|it|Cucina (attività)|ja|料理|jv|Olahan|knc|Kәmbube|ko|요리|lad|Kuzina|lfn|Cosini|lt|Pasaulio virtuvės|mr|पाककला|ms|Masakan|nap|Cucina|new|नसापहः|nl|Keuken (kookwijze)|nn|Kokekunst|pa|ਪਕਵਾਨ|pcd|Tchuisinne|pt|Culinária|ro|Cuisine|ru|Кухня (традиции)|sc|Coghina|sh|Kulinarstvo|si|සූපවේදය|simple|Cuisine|sk|Kuchárske umenie|sq|Kuzhinieria|sr|Кулинарство|sv|Matkultur|sw|Kupika|th|การครัว|tr|Mutfak (kültür)|tt|Аш-су (традицияләр)|uk|Кухня|uz|Oshxona (anʼanalar)|vi|Ẩm thực|war|Panluto|zh|菜系|zh_min_nan|Liāu-lí|zh_yue|菜系|qid=Q1778821}}." Associated deities are Kunitokotachi-no-Mikoto, Amakagami-no-Mikoto, Amayorozu-no-Mikoto, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takaokami-no-Kami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Homusubi-no-Kami}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyouke-hime-no-Kami}}.

It has four branch shrines in {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}} and is worshiped by people in culinary professions.
* Hida Takahashi Shrine ({{ill|Gero Onsen Gasshō-mura|Q11360703|qid=Q11360703}})
* Keihoku Takahashi Shrine ({{ill|Yoake no Mori|Q17209177|qid=Q17209177}} in Nakatsugawa)
* Kane Takahashi Shrine (inside Kane Shrine in Gifu)
* Hida Takayama Takahashi Shrine (inside Hie Shrine in Takayama)

===History===
According to shrine tradition, in {{ill|AD 111|Q30640|qid=Q30640}} (Keikō 41), when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258}} campaigned eastward, he invited Kunitokotachi-no-Mikoto, Amakagami-no-Mikoto, and Amayorozu-no-Mikoto here and prayed for victory. When Emperor Keikō later inspected the campaign sites, Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kashiwade no Omi}} line, was old and with imperial permission remained here. In {{ill|684|Q31128|qid=Q31128}} ({{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} 12), descendants of Iwaka Mutsukari who ruled this area were granted the surname Takahashi Ason, and in that year they merged their ancestral deity Iwaka Mutsukari at this shrine and called it Takahashi Shrine.

In {{ill|1029|Q19274|qid=Q19274}} ({{ill|Chōgen|Q1193557|qid=Q1193557}} 2), when a well was dug in the precincts, a large {{ill|Common carp|Q81110|qid=Q81110}} appeared. Reported to the capital, {{ill|Emperor Go-Ichijō|Q374087|qid=Q374087}} deemed it truly miraculous and granted the imperial plaque "Japan’s sole carp-forbidden shrine." Since then, parishioners do not eat carp, do not use vessels painted with carp, and do not raise {{ill|Koinobori|Q779745|qid=Q779745}} in May. From this comes the alternate name '''Carp Myōjin'''.

In the medieval period it was protected by the {{ill|Yūki clan|Q2975399|qid=Q2975399}} of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|Q1053695|qid=Q1053695}}. More than 20 documents remain, including donation letters, prayers, and practice records from castle lords {{ill|Yūki Masaasahi|Q11606587|qid=Q11606587}}, {{ill|Yūki Masanao|Q11606589|qid=Q11606589}}, {{ill|Yūki Masakatsu|Q8062739|qid=Q8062739}}, {{ill|Yūki Harutomo|Q8062736|qid=Q8062736}}, and {{ill|Yūki Hideyasu|Q1130929|qid=Q1130929}}. Even after Hideyasu was transferred to Echizen Fukui, ceremonial proxy visits were maintained generation after generation until the Meiji Restoration.

===Cultural properties===

=== Tochigi Prefecture designated tangible cultural property ===

* Rōmon - Donated by the Mizuno family, lords of Yūki Castle; construction took 16 years from Hōreki 4 to Meiwa 7 ({{ill|1770|Q7683|qid=Q7683}}). Restoration was carried out from 2017 to 2018.

=== Oyama City designated intangible cultural property ===

* Daidai Kagura - dedicated at the autumn annual festival.

=== Chinowa crossing ===
The chinowa ring at Takahashi Shrine has a rare square shape, about 2 m per side, not circular. The reason is unknown. It is made with one-sided reed as core, wrapped in makomo and bound with cogon-grass rope<ref>Yomiuri Shimbun Tochigi edition, August 3, 2017, p.29.</ref>.
